payload.name: ExtractExplicitActionsFromIncidentResponses
payload.description: When a user describes a past incident and explicitly lists actions they took in response, extract and preserve each specific action as event details instead of generalizing into a relationship or trait.
content: During extraction, if a message contains a direct answer to a question about what someone did (e.g., how they handled an incident), extract every explicitly named action as a separate event detail in the candidate. Do not replace the actions with a general statement about the relationship, bond, or trait.

When updating an existing memory with a message that lists specific actions, preserve the already-known event facts and add the new concrete actions; avoid changing an event memory into a relationship memory unless the message itself supports that broader category.
Prefer memory kinds that capture the action (event) over abstract kinds (relationship/profile) when the message primarily reports what the person did.

candidates.solves: Construction agents often collapse explicit behavioral details (e.g., petting, hugging, speaking calmly, slow walking) into abstract relationship statements, leaving required facts missing. This Skill applies to any future message where a speaker enumerates concrete actions in response to a question or incident; it instructs extraction to capture and retain each explicit action, while not requiring knowledge of the gold answer.

payload.name: Include all explicit activities from multi-message event narratives
payload.description: When extracting an event memory from multiple messages about the same trip, experience, or event, before composing the candidate re-read all source messages and include every explicitly mentioned activity, place, or excursion.
content: During extraction, after drafting an event memory from a multi-message conversation, scan every source message in the session for explicitly stated activities, places, or excursions. If a later message adds an activity not yet in the candidate, add it to the candidate rather than keeping only the first message's details.

Use the full message set as the source of truth for event memories; do not treat the first mention as exhaustive. When the same event is described across turns, compose a candidate that covers all explicit facts, then pass it to CRUD as a single complete ADD or UPDATE.

candidates.solves: When a construction agent condenses a multi-message travel or event narrative into one memory candidate, it may fixate on the first message and drop explicit activities stated in later messages. This rule forces re-scanning all source messages for every explicitly named activity or location before composing the candidate. It applies to any multi-message event summary where later messages add facts; it does not apply to single-message extractions or to deduplicating already-captured memories.

payload.name: ExtractExplicitObjectIdentification
payload.description: When a speaker explicitly identifies what an object, picture, map, or other item is, create a memory candidate capturing that item and its explicit description.
content: During extraction, if a message explicitly states what an object or visual is (phrases like 'It's a map of...' or 'This is a photo of...'), generate a candidate memory for that item and its stated subject/content.
Do not skip such statements because the message also contains enthusiasm or background detail; preserve the factual identification in a compact memory tied to the speaker and context.

candidates.solves: Construction extraction sometimes omits factual statements that explicitly identify an object or visual because the same message also contains subjective reactions or background detail. This skill applies to future sessions whenever a speaker states what a shown item is, ensuring the item's explicit subject or content is captured as a memory instead of being dropped.

payload.name: Aggregate repeated event counts in memory
payload.description: When constructing memories from a message that reports another instance of an event already recorded for the same subject, use this Skill to store an explicit cumulative count.
content: During extraction, if an utterance describes an event that is another occurrence of an event type already present in the memory pool (signaled by 'another', 'again', 'second time', etc.), extract not only the new event but also a compact state memory stating the total count so far (e.g., 'has been rejected N times').

During CRUD, before committing a new repeated event, retrieve existing memories for the same subject and event type; then ADD a new state memory with the cumulative count or UPDATE/MERGE an existing state memory to increment the count and note the latest occurrence. Keep event memories for individual occurrences and do not overwrite their world_start dates.

candidates.solves: The failure mode is that construction records each occurrence as an isolated event, leaving count-based questions only partially answerable by inference. This Skill abstracts the required aggregation rule: whenever a new message signals another instance of a known event type, the memory must explicitly store the cumulative count. It applies to any recurring countable event in future sessions (e.g., submissions, rejections, wins, relocations) where a later question may ask 'how many times'.

payload.name: Preserve named item type when summarizing a collection or line
payload.description: When a message mentions a line, collection, or range and explicitly names the concrete item type, include that specific item type in the extracted memory candidate instead of only paraphrasing the broad line.
content: During extraction, if a speaker says something is part of a limited-edition line, collection, or product range and also names the specific item (e.g., 'this hoodie is from my own collection', 'made a limited edition line of shirts'), record the named item type in the candidate content.
Retain the 'from my own collection' or 'not for sale' context when it explains origin or exclusivity, as it is often needed to answer promotion, inventory, or business-history questions.
Apply during candidate extraction; ADD or UPDATE the event memory with the specific noun, and do not infer item types that are not explicitly mentioned.

candidates.solves: A message explicitly names an item type (e.g., hoodie) while describing it as part of a limited-edition line or collection, but the extracted candidate paraphrases only the broader line and drops the concrete noun, making later recall of the specific item partial. The reusable fix is to preserve any explicitly named item type whenever a line/collection/range is summarized, because future questions will target that concrete noun. This applies across domains (clothing, food, products, art) and should not be used to infer item types that were not stated.

payload.name: PreserveDistinctExplicitActivitiesInExtraction
payload.description: When extracting or updating memories from a dialogue message that mentions multiple distinct activities, plans, or creative intentions, preserve each explicit action rather than collapsing them into a general impression.
content: During extraction, if one message contains several distinct explicit actions, plans, or creative intentions, create a candidate for each or include all of them explicitly; do not replace concrete activities with a vague phrase like 'gets deep in thought'.

Before finalizing a candidate, re-read the source message and confirm every explicit activity or intention mentioned by the speaker is represented; if any is missing, revise the candidate rather than relying on later updates.
During CRUD, when merging or updating memories, keep distinct explicit activities as separate memory entries unless the evidence clearly supports collapsing them without losing information.

candidates.solves: The diagnosed cause is that extraction over-compressed a message containing a concrete creative plan into a vague inner-state summary, dropping the explicit plan. The reusable mechanism is over-compression of multi-part utterances during memory extraction. This applies whenever a single message states multiple distinct activities or intentions and a draft candidate would lose one; it does not apply to inferring unstated facts.

payload.name: ExtractGeneralPreferenceAlongsideConcreteEvent
payload.description: When a message states a general preference or habitual activity and then gives a specific instance, extract the general statement as a preference and the specific instance as an event.
content: During extraction, when a message contains a general, ongoing preference or habit (e.g., 'we love to discover new places to eat') and also a concrete instance, record the general statement as a separate `preference` memory and the concrete instance as an `event` memory—both are independently durable.

During CRUD, before merging a new specific instance into an existing event memory, check if the originating message also stated a general preference; if that preference is missing from memory, add it (as a new memory or enrichment) so the general fact is not lost.

candidates.solves: Construction extraction often drops a general preference or habitual activity when the same utterance also gives a concrete example, leaving memory that only records the specific event. This Skill ensures both the general preference (as `preference`) and the specific event are captured, and that CRUD updates check for the missing general preference. It applies whenever a user states an ongoing interest and a particular instance in the same or later turn.

payload.name: Persist containing region for location events
payload.description: When constructing memories from a message that names a city or place, also extract its confidently known state/province/country so region-level questions can be answered.
content: During extraction, when a message mentions a specific city, town, or landmark, include its confidently known containing state/province/country in the same memory candidate rather than storing only the local place name.

During CREATE/UPDATE/MERGE enrichment, if adding a location detail to an existing memory, also add the containing region of that detail when confidently known, so the memory can support state-level and country-level queries.
Only add the containing region when it follows from established geographic knowledge; do not guess or infer regions from context that is not entailed.

candidates.solves: A location-bearing event was stored only with the city name, leaving later state/country-level claims unsupported. The mechanism is that place names entail a containing administrative region that should be persisted alongside the event. This applies to extraction and enrichment whenever a confidently known state/province/country exists for a mentioned place; it does not apply to invented or unverifiable locations.

payload.name: extract_reported_third_party_assessments
payload.description: When extracting memories from a message where one person reports what a third party (e.g., doctor, expert) said about another person's condition or situation, create a separate state candidate for that reported assessment even if other candidates cover the general topic.
content: If a message contains a reported statement from a third party (e.g., 'The doctor said...') about someone's condition or status, extract that assessment as its own state memory, distinct from any state about the person's general situation and from any relationship memories.

Use the person whose condition is being assessed as the subject, and phrase the memory to record the assessment (e.g., 'Doctor assessed X's injury as not too serious.'), with world_start set to the message timestamp.
Do not merge this assessment into a broader state or relationship candidate; keep it as a separate durable fact.

candidates.solves: During extraction, when a speaker reports a third-party assessment (e.g., 'the doctor said...') about another person's condition, the model may capture only the general situation and support relationship, omitting the specific evaluative fact. This Skill applies to future conversations with reported professional/medical judgments about someone's state, where the judgment is a distinct durable fact even inside a supportive message. It does not apply to first-person statements or purely emotional support without an external assessment.

payload.name: Preserve compound topics during memory extraction
payload.description: When a message explicitly lists multiple topics or items (e.g., 'A and B', 'A, B, and C'), include all named items when creating a memory from that message; do not drop any element during summarization or paraphrase.
content: During extraction, when the speaker explicitly names multiple topics or items (e.g., 'dreams and life', 'A, B, and C'), preserve every named item in the memory candidate content; do not paraphrase or merge them into a single broader term.
If the final memory content omits any item that the source message explicitly listed, revise the candidate (or issue an UPDATE) so the memory retains the full set.

candidates.solves: The extraction summarized 'dreams and life' as 'reflecting on life', dropping an explicitly named element, so the memory partially covered the claim. Compound phrases are paraphrased too aggressively during candidate generation, losing items. This rule applies whenever a message enumerates multiple topics that a memory should retain.

payload.name: ExtractExplicitImportanceStatements
payload.description: When a message explicitly states that something is important or valued to the user, extract that as a separate durable preference memory in addition to any event or activity memory.
content: During extraction, if a message contains an explicit importance/value statement (e.g., 'X is really important to me', 'I value X', 'X matters a lot'), always create a preference memory capturing 'X is important to [user]' even when the same message also describes an activity or event.
Do not embed the importance only inside an event memory; preserve it as a standalone preference so later questions about the value can be answered.
During update or enrichment, if a later message reveals an explicit importance that existing memories only imply, add a preference memory for that importance statement.

candidates.solves: When a person explicitly states that something is important to them (e.g., 'X is really important to me', 'I value X', 'X matters a lot'), extraction often records only the accompanying activity and loses the explicit importance claim. This causes later questions about that value to fail. The fix is to always extract explicit importance statements as standalone preference memories, separate from any event memory, so the declared value is preserved and answerable.

payload.name: ExtractDistinctFactsFromSingleTurn
payload.description: When a single user message contains multiple distinct durable facts or events, use this skill during extraction to create separate candidates instead of collapsing them into one memory.
content: During candidate extraction, parse each user turn for every distinct durable fact. If a single message contains multiple independent facts (e.g., a trip and a separate breakdown), emit one candidate per fact rather than one combined candidate.

During CRUD operations, keep distinct durable facts from such candidates in separate memory entries unless they are causally inseparable; do not let one memorable event overshadow another explicit claim from the same message.

candidates.solves: During extraction, a multi-fact user utterance was collapsed into one event candidate, omitting an explicit breakdown and leaving it unanswerable. The fix is to emit separate candidates for independent durable facts in the same turn. This applies whenever one message states multiple separable facts (events, breakdowns, purchases, plans); it does not apply to splitting a single cohesive event or merging inseparable details.

payload.name: Capture-Confirmed-Ordinal-Facts
payload.description: When a user confirms a specific fact from a prior question, include it and its timing in extracted memory candidates.
content: During extraction, treat an affirmative answer to a direct question as explicit confirmation of the fact asserted in that question; add that fact to the relevant memory candidate even if the follow-up utterance only expands on it.

When the confirmed fact refers to a numbered work or occurrence (e.g., 'third one', 'second time'), store the ordinal value and the session/message date as the associated time in the event or profile memory.

candidates.solves: The diagnosed cause was extraction summarizing a user's reply while dropping an ordinal and date confirmed by the previous question. This rule generalizes the mechanism of treating Q&A confirmations as explicit evidence and preserving ordinal/temporal attributes when extracting memories. It applies to future construction sessions where a fact is stated across adjacent turns, not where the fact requires inference absent from the conversation.

payload.name: Capture explicit substitutions from recommendations
payload.description: Use during extraction when a message responds to a request with specific named options or substitutes; ensure each concrete alternative is preserved in the memory content.
content: When extracting from a message that lists concrete substitutions or alternatives (e.g., 'use A or B instead of X'), include those named options in the memory content rather than summarizing only the general topic or offer to help.

candidates.solves: When a speaker answers a direct question with concrete alternatives or substitutions, extraction often records only the general topic or offer of help and loses the specific options. This rule instructs construction to preserve the explicit named alternatives so future questions about the specific substitution can be answered. It applies to messages containing specific recommendations, not to general statements of interest or intent.

payload.name: Extract First-Person Claims as Subject Memories
payload.description: Use when a dialogue contains a first-person statement about a speaker's own feelings, body, habits, or routines; extract it as a subject-specific memory rather than a conversation summary.
content: During extraction, if a speaker says something about their own feelings, habits, routines, or body (e.g., 'Exercise makes me feel connected to my body'), create a separate memory with subject = speaker and the specific claim.
Do not fold such first-person statements into a generic conversation summary; preserve them as concrete, queryable memories.
Verify the memory subject matches the actual speaker to avoid misattributing statements to another participant.

candidates.solves: The diagnosed failure was an extraction candidate summarizing a whole conversation and losing a specific first-person claim about exercise. The abstract mechanism is over-general summarization that omits concrete self-referential facts. This rule counteracts that by requiring subject-specific memories for first-person statements, and applies to any future dialogue where a participant discloses personal feelings, preferences, or routines.

payload.name: Complete-enumeration-in-memory-extraction
payload.description: When a source message enumerates multiple distinct items (advice, preferences, attributes, goals), ensure all are captured in the extracted or merged memory, not just the first subset.
content: When processing a message that explicitly lists multiple distinct items (e.g., 'X, Y, and Z', bullet points, or 'also'), extract every item. Do not truncate the list based on perceived relevance or order.

Represent the full set either as separate memory candidates per item or as one candidate containing the complete enumeration; if merging with an existing memory, ensure the merged memory still contains all distinct items.

Before finalizing an ADD/UPDATE/MERGE, verify the candidate or resulting memory covers every distinct item present in the source evidence; if any item is missing, correct the candidate or issue the appropriate update.

candidates.solves: The failed diagnosis showed an extraction candidate dropping the last item of a three-part advice list, leaving memory incomplete and a reference claim missing. This Skill addresses the general mechanism of incomplete extraction from enumerated lists, applying whenever a message presents multiple distinct durable items that should all be stored. It does not apply when the enumeration is illustrative rather than exhaustive, or when the message explicitly prioritizes a single item.

payload.name: Extract every listed durable activity
payload.description: Use during candidate extraction when a single user message lists multiple distinct activities, facts, or experiences; create a candidate for each, not only the most prominent one.
content: When a message enumerates multiple distinct activities or facts (e.g., separated by commas or 'and'), extract one candidate per listed item that is durable and relevant, even if one item seems more significant.

Do not collapse an enumerated list into a single memory that drops secondary items; if items share a theme, either keep them as separate memories or explicitly include all items in the memory content.

candidates.solves: A construction extraction failure occurred because a message listing several career-development activities (studying, workshops, networking, conference presentation) yielded only one memory for the conference, so the workshop fact was lost. The reusable mechanism is selective extraction of one salient item from an enumeration. Apply during extraction whenever a single user message contains multiple distinct durable facts, even when one seems more prominent; the rule does not apply to merging or updating existing memories.

payload.name: Preserve-all-alternatives-in-extraction
payload.description: When extracting a memory from a message that lists multiple alternatives (e.g., 'or', 'and', comma-separated options), capture every listed option; do not drop any item.
content: During extraction, if a message names multiple alternative options, suggestions, or list items connected by 'or', 'and', or commas, the candidate memory content must include every listed item, not only the first or most prominent one.
Before finalizing a candidate, scan the full message for enumerated alternatives and verify that each one is represented in the content; a later query may target any individual item.

When updating an existing memory, if the source message still supports an alternative that is present in the current memory, do not remove that alternative unless the source explicitly retracts or contradicts it.

candidates.solves: Diagnosed failure: an extraction candidate captured only 'biking' from a message suggesting 'biking or using public transport', so the memory lacked the public transport option and the claim was MISSING. The rule to preserve all alternatives in a single message transfers to any future input containing lists, options, or suggestions with multiple items, preventing partial memory extractions.

payload.name: Preserve compound enumerated items in extraction
payload.description: When a memory is being extracted or updated from a statement listing multiple activities, roles, topics, or objects joined by 'and' or commas, include every listed item; do not let an explanatory clause reduce the memory to only the first or most prominent item.
content: During extraction, if a statement presents several items as true parts of the same fact or event (A and B, or A, B, and C), explicitly store every item; treat a purpose/explanation phrase that mentions one item as evidence that all mentioned items belong to that fact.

During CRUD, when a candidate or existing memory has captured only one item from such a compound enumeration, UPDATE or MERGE to add the missing items, keeping the memory linked to the same source evidence.

candidates.solves: Extraction may capture only the first item of an 'A and B' construction when the second item appears inside a purpose or explanation clause, leaving later questions about B unanswered. This Skill requires every conjunct named as true for the same event or fact to be stored explicitly. It applies to future statements listing activities, roles, topics, or objects with 'and' or commas, but not to disjunctive alternatives or uncertain options.

payload.name: Preserve explicit source or discovery detail with event memories
payload.description: When extracting or updating a memory of an event and the speaker also states how they learned about or discovered it (e.g., saw a flyer, heard from a friend, read online), include that source/discovery detail in the memory content.
content: During extraction, if a statement contains both an event and the explicit way the person learned about, found, or discovered that event, preserve the source/discovery detail in the same memory or as a separate linked memory; do not record only the event outcome.
When updating an existing event memory, carry forward any explicit source/discovery detail from the original or new evidence, adding it to the memory content instead of dropping it.

candidates.solves: The diagnosed cause is that extraction recorded an event (signing up for a workshop) but omitted the explicitly stated discovery mechanism (saw a flyer). The abstract failure is losing the 'how the person learned about it' detail when an event and its source are mentioned together. The proposed rule preserves explicit source/discovery details in memory, making later 'how did X hear about Y' questions answerable. It applies to any future extraction or update where a speaker states how they learned about, found, or discovered an event.
